fact: Milliken caps a residence at 3 dogs aged 4 months or older unless the Town Administrator grants a permit that is not likely to create a nuisance or disturb the neighborhood.
quote: Subject to the provisions of Subsection (e) of this Section, no person shall maintain more than three (3) dogs which are four (4) or more months old per residence within the Town, and the owning of more than three (3) such dogs per residence is hereby declared to be a nuisance. This shall not apply to those portions of the Town where the zoning of the property would permit a greater number of animals to be kept. … The Town Administrator may grant a permit only in those instances in which all of the requirements in subsection (a) above have been met and the granting of the permit is not likely to create a nuisance or disturb the neighborhood.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Secs. 7-5-50(d)–(e) and 7-5-60(b), Animal Control (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through Municode's content API (product 18077, job 492897 = Supp. No. 22, Update 1). 7-5-60(e): a granted permit may be reviewed annually or at any time by the Town Administrator.

fact: Milliken requires a pet to be kept securely enclosed in a pen or building and bars letting any place where animals are kept become foul, malodorous or unwholesome.
quote: Pets. No person who owns any pet within the Town shall fail to keep such pet securely enclosed in a pen or building, and no such person shall permit such pet to run or fly at will except on the premises of such person, or to go upon the premises of another person. … Animal safety. No person who keeps any animal within the Town shall permit the place within which animals are kept to become foul, noisome, putrid, malodorous, unwholesome, offensive or in any way dangerous or detrimental to animal's health, comfort or general welfare.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 7-5-90(d) and (f), Regulation of animals (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The code does not say whether a fenced backyard counts as a "pen"; pages hedge it.

fact: Milliken bars running a kennel or any place for training, boarding or breeding animals without a permit from the Town.
quote: Training, boarding or breeding of animals prohibited. Unless a permit is obtained under Section 7-5-60, no person shall keep, maintain or operate within the Town any kennel, building or other place or establishment for the purpose of training, boarding or breeding of animals, including the keeping, maintaining or operating of such an establishment.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 7-5-90(b), Regulation of animals (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The Land Use Code separately lists "Animal boarding including day care" among uses in some commercial and industrial districts (Art. II).

fact: Milliken lets a dog left alone be tethered on a trolley or cable run at least 10 feet long, mounted 4 to 7 feet above the ground, and caps tethering at 10 hours in any 24.
quote: The trolley system or cable run must be at least ten (10) feet in length and mounted at least four (4) feet and no more than seven (7) feet above ground level. … The tethered domesticated animal shall be provided with sufficient area to exercise, and shall have access to adequate shelter and adequate water. … In no case shall a domesticated animal be tethered in excess of ten (10) hours in a twenty-four-hour period.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 7-5-90(h), Tethering of domesticated animal (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). 7-5-90(h)(3)g also allows a flush stake with a freely rotating ring under the same conditions, less the height rule.

fact: Milliken requires an owner to pick up and dispose of an animal's waste right away on public property and on anyone else's private property.
quote: Removal of fecal matter. Any owner taking a domesticated animal to any public way or other public property in the Town shall immediately remove, or cause to be removed, and lawfully dispose of all fecal matter left on such property by the domesticated animal. Any owner, taking any domesticated animal upon any private property other than his or her own, shall immediately remove, or cause to be removed, and lawfully dispose of all fecal matter left on such property by the animal.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 7-5-90(e), Removal of fecal matter (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897).

fact: Milliken requires a yearly Town license for every dog 6 months or older, and rabies vaccination every 3 years for dogs and cats that age.
quote: Every owner of a dog or cat six (6) months of age or older shall have such dog or cat vaccinated every three (3) years against rabies with a Colorado Department of Health-approved vaccine by a licensed veterinarian. … No person shall own any dog six (6) months of age or older without obtaining and keeping in force a valid license therefor in the manner provided in this Section. … Such license shall be in effect for a period of one (1) year from the date of issuance. … Each application for a dog license shall be made to the Town Clerk upon a form provided for that purpose. At the time the completed application is submitted to the Town Clerk, the applicant shall submit the certificate of vaccination required by Section 7-5-20 above, and shall pay the required license fee.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Secs. 7-5-20 and 7-5-30, Rabies vaccination and dog license (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). Applications go to the Town Clerk with the vaccination certificate (7-5-30(b)).

fact: Milliken requires a fence permit before construction, prohibits chain-link fencing outside industrial districts except approved replacements in the original town plat, limits front-yard fences to 42 inches and rear privacy fences to 7 feet, and applies these fence rules to existing houses too.
quote: A fence permit is required prior to the start of construction. … Fences used in front yards and adjacent to public streets, open space, or parks along a side or rear yard shall be at least fifty (50%) percent open. … Chain-link fencing with or without slats shall be prohibited, except within an industrial zoning district pursuant to paragraph (6)(f) below, or as administratively approved for replacement or extension of existing chain-link fencing within the Plat of the Town of Milliken Subdivision on residential property in close proximity to existing chain-link fencing within the neighborhood. … No more than forty-two (42) inches high between the front building line and the front property line. … No more than seven (7) feet high for an opaque privacy fence located on a rear property line or on a side yard line in the rear yard. … (c) Existing detached single unit dwellings and two-family dwellings shall be exempt from the standards in this Division 3, except that landscaping for such dwellings shall comply with the prohibited plant species provisions in Section 16-3-345(f), the maintenance requirements in Section 16-3-375(c), and the fence and wall standards in Section 16-3-390.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Secs. 16-3-390(b), Fences and Walls, and 16-3-305(c), Applicability (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). 16-3-305(c) keeps these fence standards in force for existing detached homes and duplexes, which are otherwise exempt from Division 3. The code does not say whether freestanding kennel panels count as fencing; pages hedge it.

fact: Milliken requires any retaining wall taller than 48 inches to be engineered and approved in advance by the Town Engineer and Building Official.
quote: Retaining Walls. Retaining walls shall be designed to resist loads due to the lateral pressure of retained material in accordance with accepted engineering practice and shall not be unsightly or detrimental to abutting property. Any retaining wall greater than forty-eight (48) inches in height shall be engineered and allowed only with prior approval from the Town Engineer and Building Official.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-390(b)(5), Retaining Walls (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). Part of the fence and wall standards that 16-3-305(c) keeps in force for existing homes.

fact: Milliken lets an accessory building or structure of 120 square feet or less go up without a building permit.
quote: Accessory buildings and structures which are not any larger than one hundred twenty (120) square feet in area, as measured around the perimeter of the building shall be permitted without a building permit.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-500(a), Accessory Buildings and Structures (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The code does not say whether a playset or a putting green is an accessory structure; pages hedge it.

fact: Milliken's landscape table requires new single-family and two-family front yards, and side or rear yards next to parks, open space or a public street, to be at least 50 percent live materials at maturity.
quote: Front yard landscape must include a minimum of 50 percent live materials at maturity between the front of the principal building and the curb; additional landscape/xeriscape is encouraged … Side or rear yards adjacent to parks, open space, or public street: Minimum of 50 percent live materials at maturity
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-315(c), Table 16-3-3-1, single-family and two-family column (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897), table cells parsed by column. Division 3 applies to new development (16-3-305(a)); existing detached homes and duplexes are exempt (16-3-305(c), see milliken-code-16-3-303-nonfunctional).

fact: For nonresidential sites, Milliken's landscape table asks for at least 15 percent of the site landscaped, 75 percent live materials at maturity, and irrigated turf grass in active recreation areas.
quote: Minimum 15 percent of the gross site area shall be landscaped Generally: 75 percent live materials at maturity; 50 percent of which shall be between the front of the building and the curb For active recreation areas: Establish irrigated turf grass Non-recreation areas: Use native grasses where appropriate
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-315(c), Table 16-3-3-1, nonresidential column (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897), table cells parsed by column. The table does not say whether functional artificial turf may stand in for irrigated turf grass on an active recreation area; pages hedge it and send the reader to Milliken Planning.

fact: Milliken caps high-water turf grass at 50 percent of the required landscaped area for residential uses and 20 percent for other uses, with parks and open space exempt.
quote: Single-family and multifamily residential uses. The total amount of high-water turf grass shall not exceed more than fifty (50%) percent of the required landscaped area. (2) All other uses. The total amount of high-water turf grass shall not exceed more than twenty percent (20%) of the required landscaped area. Exemptions. Parks and open space shall be exempt from the turf grass limitations in paragraphs (1) and (2) above. High-water turf grass is discouraged in those areas.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-335(b), Water Efficiency in Landscape Design (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). These caps are on living grass; the code does not mention artificial turf here.

fact: For parking lots of 25 or more spaces, Milliken requires islands at least 8 feet wide and 125 square feet and prohibits turf grass in any area narrower than 8 feet.
quote: All parking lots with twenty-five (25) spaces or more shall be subject to these requirements. … Trees shall be grouped in parking lot islands. … Parking lot islands shall be a minimum of eight (8) feet wide and shall be a minimum size of one hundred twenty-five (125) square feet. … Ground Cover. Irrigated turf grass shall be limited. Turf grass is prohibited in areas less than eight (8) feet wide.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-365, Parking Lot Landscaping Standards (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897).

fact: Outside detached homes and duplexes, Milliken requires older landscaping to meet current standards once changes reach more than 25 percent of the landscaped area on the last approved site plan, counted cumulatively.
quote: Except for detached single-unit dwellings and two-family dwellings, any legal nonconforming landscaping must comply with these regulations if changes are made to more than twenty-five (25%) percent of the total landscaped area of the subject property. Such twenty-five (25%) percent total landscaped area will be measured from the most recently approved site plan for the property. (b) Any subsequent request, application, or permit for such improvements to landscaped area on the same commercial, industrial, or multifamily property shall be cumulative to any prior request, application, or permit.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-310, Nonconforming Landscaping (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). Separate from the state turf law's redevelopment test (co-sb24-005-redevelopment), which 16-3-303 adopts by reference.

fact: Since January 1, 2026, Milliken has barred nonfunctional artificial turf in new development and redevelopment on multifamily properties with more than 12 units, as well as on commercial, HOA common and right-of-way property, using the state law's definitions as amended.
quote: Definitions. For purposes of this section, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth in section 37-99-102, C.R.S., as it may be from time to time amended … Notwithstanding any other provision in this Code to the contrary, commencing on and after January 1, 2026, no person shall install, plant or place any nonfunctional turf, nonfunctional artificial turf, or invasive plant species as part of a new development project or redevelopment project on any: (1) Commercial, institutional, or industrial property; (2) Common interest community property; (3) Street right-of-way, parking lot, median, or transportation corridor; or (4) Multifamily residential housing premises property that includes more than twelve (12) dwelling units. (Ord. 831, § 1, 12-22-2025)
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-3-303 (Ord. 831, Dec. 22, 2025; codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The state law reaches multifamily common areas only from January 1, 2028 (co-hb25-1113-multifamily-2028); Milliken's section lists them with no later date. Because the definitions follow C.R.S. 37-99-102 "as amended", HB25-1113's functional-artificial-turf definition applies.

fact: Milliken's R-1 single-family district allows sporting courts, tennis courts, pools and other similar structures by right only in the rear yard, and caps lot coverage at 40 percent.
quote: Accessory buildings and structures not exceeding forty (40) percent lot coverage, only one (1) may exceed seven hundred twenty (720) square feet. … Sporting courts, tennis courts, swimming pools and other similar structures provided they are located in the rear yard of the lot. … Maximum Lot Coverage: 40%. … Minimum Rear Setback: Twenty (20) feet.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-2-110, Single-Family Residential (R-1), as amended by Ord. 830, Nov. 24, 2025 (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The code does not name putting greens; whether a green is a "similar structure" is unsettled, so pages hedge it and send the reader to Milliken Planning. R-2 and R-1E carry similar lists.

fact: Milliken counts buildings and structures toward lot coverage and leaves out flat surfaces such as sidewalks, driveways and uncovered patios.
quote: Lot coverage means the total square footage of all buildings and structures on the lot. Flat surfaces, such as sidewalks, driveways and uncovered patios are not included when calculating lot coverage.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-8-200, Definitions, "Lot coverage" (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The definition does not name turf or a putting green; flat turf reads like the listed flat surfaces, but that is an inference, and pages hedge it.

fact: Milliken requires new subdivisions to build a one-acre pocket park for every 250 homes, with live ground cover, trees and irrigation plus playground equipment or another amenity, owned and maintained by the HOA or the landowner; a smaller project near a neighborhood park pays cash in lieu of its share.
quote: Developers must provide the land and develop a one-acre pocket park for every two hundred fifty (250) residential units. At a minimum, a pocket park shall include live ground cover, trees, and irrigation plus one (1) of the following: playground equipment, contemplative garden or other active or passive recreation opportunities for the neighborhood, as approved by the Town. (2) Projects with less than two hundred fifty (250) units must provide a pocket park or demonstrate that they are within one-half (½) mile of a neighborhood park. If credit is taken for proximity to a neighborhood park, the developer must provide a cash-in-lieu equivalent for its pro rata share of the cost of land and improvements for a pocket park … (4) Pocket parks, landscaped outlots and private recreational facilities shall be owned and maintained by a homeowners' association or the landowner.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-5-405(e), Park, Open space, and Trail Requirements (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). The code does not say whether the surfacing under play equipment may be artificial turf, or whether turf counts toward "live ground cover" (it would not on its face); pages hedge it. Re-read 2026-09-25: the ownership clause is 16-5-405(e)(4), not (9); the cash-in-lieu sentence of (e)(2) added to the quote.

fact: Milliken lets a state-licensed family childcare home run as a home occupation once it has Town zoning approval, and bars altering a property's exterior for the purpose of a home occupation.
quote: The exterior of the property cannot be altered for the purpose of operating a home occupation, nor can the existence of a home occupation affect the residential character of the neighborhood. … Home occupations may include state-licensed family childcare homes (residential day care facilities) that have received zoning approval from the Town. (10) Home Occupations shall obtain a business license as required by the Town prior to commencement of operation.
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Sec. 16-4-210(a), Home Occupations (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). Whether turfing a backyard play yard counts as altering the exterior "for the purpose of" the home occupation is not addressed; pages hedge it.

fact: In Milliken's R-1 single-family district a childcare center, which the code defines as a state-licensed facility that is not a residence, is a conditional use rather than a use by right.
quote: Conditional Uses. a. Adult care, day care centers, and senior centers. … d. Childcare centers. … Childcare center means a facility that is not a residence, is licensed by the State, and is maintained for the whole or part of a day for the care of children under the age of sixteen (16) years not related to the owner, operator or manager thereof
source_label: Milliken Municipal Code Secs. 16-2-110(b)(2) and 16-8-200, "Childcare center" (codified through Ord. No. 838, March 25, 2026)
notes: Read through Municode's content API (job 492897). Childcare centers are also conditional in R-1E and R-2 and appear among uses in the commercial districts.

fact: The Mad Russian Golf Course in Milliken is a public 18-hole, par-71 course built in 1987 and known for small, demanding greens.
quote: Mad Russian Golf & Country Club's small and difficult greens are demanding and they will test your iron play. Be prepared to utilize your best short game skills on this course. Holes 18 Par 71 Length 5889 yds … Type Public … Year Built 1987
source_label: GolfPass course directory, Mad Russian Golf Course, Milliken, Colorado
notes: A golf directory, so EXTERNAL_SOURCE; the operator's own page (trpr.org) blocks automated fetch. Colorado AvidGolfer lists the same par, holes and 1987 date and names Bob Ehrlich as designer. The U.S. Census geocoder (checked 2026-09-25) places the course address on Country Club Parkway inside Milliken town.

fact: Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District, an independent district organized in 1994, took on the Mad Russian Golf Course under a 25-year agreement that began January 1, 2023.
quote: Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District is an independent governmental entity organized in April 1994, under the provisions of the Colorado Revised Statutes. … On January 1, 2023, the District entered into a twenty five-year right to use asset agreement for the Mad Russian Golf Course.
source_label: Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District, 2023 audited financial statements, Notes 1 and 4 (filed with the Colorado Division of Local Government)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 (pdftotext). The same report lists the Milliken Athletic Complex and a second pool in Milliken among district facilities. Dollar figures in the report are left out of the pages on purpose.

fact: Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District's Milliken facilities include the Milliken Athletic Complex, the Mad Russian Golf Course and event center, and a second pool added in 2023.
quote: The district experienced exciting growth in 2023 including the addition of the Mad Russian Golf Course, event center, and second pool in Milliken. … the lease collateralized by the Nelson Ballfield property, Milliken Athletic Complex and land, and the Mad Russian Golf Course and event center.
source_label: Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District, 2023 audited financial statements, Management's Discussion and Analysis (filed with the Colorado Division of Local Government)
notes: Read 2026-09-25. Where the Nelson Ballfield sits is not stated, so pages name only the Milliken Athletic Complex.

fact: The Town of Milliken points residents to Thompson Rivers Parks and Recreation District for youth and adult sports, recreation programs and the Milliken Sports Complex.
quote: Local youth and adult sports, recreation programs and other youth events are offered by Thompson River Parks and Recreation District (TRPR) . … For recreation programs and information about the Milliken Sports Complex (MAC) contact the Thompson River Parks and Recreation (TRPR)
source_label: Town of Milliken, Parks & Lakes
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The page also lists the Town's park rules (see milliken-co.parks-off-leash).

fact: Milliken's park rules allow off-leash dogs only at the Milliken Dog Park and ask owners to bag dog waste at the litter stations.
quote: Dogs: No off-leash dogs are permitted in parks, except for the Milliken Dog Park. Properly dispose of dog waste in trash receptacles using materials provided at litter stations.
source_label: Town of Milliken, Parks & Lakes (Park Use Rules)
notes: Read 2026-09-25. Posted park rules, not a code section.

fact: The Milliken Dog Park, at County Road 25 and Highway 60 on the east side of town, has separate grassy areas for large and smaller dogs, water, litter bags and a covered area.
quote: Milliken Dog Park is located on the east side of town on the corner of CR 25 and Highway 60. Managed by the Milliken Parks Department. Park Features Large grassy area for large dogs Large grassy area for smaller dogs Water Litter bags Covered Area for Humans Benches No Restroom Facility
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Milliken Dog Park

fact: Lola Park, Milliken's oldest and most used park, had its shelters and playground equipment replaced in 2016.
quote: Lola Park is located on Forest Street, between Irene and Josephine Avenue. It is Milliken's oldest and most used park. In 2016 Lola Park Shelters and Playground Equipment were replaced. Both shelters are equipped with electricity.
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Lola Park

fact: Florence Park in the Frank Farms subdivision has playground structures on a pea gravel base beside a large open play area.
quote: Florence Park is located in the Frank Farms Subdivision on Holly Street between Rachel Avenue and Tamera Avenue. Managed by the Milliken Parks Department. Park Features Playground Structures with Pea Gravel Base Large Open Space for Play
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Florence Park
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The only Town park page that names its playground surface.

fact: Ada Park, south of Highway 60, has swing sets with 6 swings, a teeter totter and a tot play structure.
quote: Ada Park is located south of Hwy 60 on Aragon Ct. Managed by: Milliken Parks Department Park Features Playground Equipment Swing Set Structures with 6 Swings Teeter Totter Tot Play Structure with Picnic Tables
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Ada Park
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The shelter-fee table on the same page defines a resident as someone living in the RE-5J School District.

fact: Sappington Park, in the center of Settlers Village beside Knowledge Quest Academy, has soccer fields and a large grassy area that the school's students use at recess and in physical education.
quote: Sappington Park is located in the center of Settlers Village, next to Knowledge Quest Academy on School House Drive. … This park plays host to our Annual Easter Eggstravaganza and has been a great addition to KQA, whose students utilize the large area during recess and physical education activities. … Park Features Soccer Fields Walking Trails BBQ Grill Gazebo & Picnic Area Large Grassy area
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Sappington Park
notes: Read 2026-09-25. Partly funded by a Great Outdoors Colorado grant, per the same page.

fact: Ehrlich Park and Lake in the Colony Point subdivision has a playground, a walking trail and a fishing dock.
quote: Ehrlich Park & Lake is located in Colony Point Subdivision off of S. Traildust Drive. Managed by: Milliken Parks Department Park Features Playground and Equipment Walking Trail Fishing Dock Restroom Facility
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Ehrlich Park & Lake

fact: Kids and Cops Park, at Broad Street and North Ethel Avenue next to the Police Department, has playground and fitness equipment.
quote: Kids and Cops Park is located at the corner of Broad St. and N Ethel Avenue next to the Police Department. Managed by Milliken Parks Department. Park Features Playground and Equipment Fitness Equipment Benches No Restroom Facility
source_label: Town of Milliken, Facilities: Kids & Cops Park

fact: Settlers Village's recorded covenants allow no more than 3 dogs and 3 cats per owner and require Architectural Review Committee approval for a dog run, which may not be visible from a street or public view.
quote: No Owner may keep more than three (3) dogs and three (3) cats. Household pets shall not be permitted to roam freely around the properties and shall be kept under the strict supervision and control of their Owners at all times. … Clothes Lines and Dog Runs. No clothes lines shall be located on any Lot and dog runs must first be approved by the Architectural Review Committee and shall not be located on any Lot where they are visible from a street or public view.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Settlers Village Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 9 (recorded Aug. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2877827)
notes: The HOA posts a scanned copy; read 2026-09-25 by OCR of the recorded pages (one OCR misread, "lacated", corrected to "located"). The HOA site lists two CC&R amendments; the one readable (Reception No. 3314114, 2005) covers only fencing on Block 17 Replat lots 2–18.

fact: Settlers Village's covenants require written Architectural Review Committee approval before any structure or improvement, fences and landscaping included, is built or changed.
quote: No buildings, structures or other improvements including fences and landscaping shall be constructed, modified or altered unless first approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Settlers Village Subdivision, Art. XI, Sec. 2 (recorded Aug. 27, 2001, Weld County Reception No. 2877827)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 by OCR of the recorded scan the HOA posts. Builders with Declarant approval were exempt during construction and sales.

fact: The Settlers Village architectural application asks for plans, specifications, color or material samples, or photographs, and commits the owner to no work until written approval arrives.
quote: ONE OF THE FOLLOWING MUST BE SUBMITTED BEFORE YOUR REQUEST WILL BE REVIEWED: Plans including location, elevations, and dimensions Specifications (e.g. manufacturer's brochure) Samples of colors Samples or description of materials Photographs … No work or commitment of work will be made by me until I have received written approval from the Association.
source_label: Settlers Village HOA, Application for Approval of Architectural Improvement
notes: Read 2026-09-25 (text PDF).
